page.text:
Addition $+ : \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is defined
recursively on the first argument:
$$\begin{aligned}
0 + m &:= m \\
S(k) + m &:= S(k + m)
\end{aligned}$$
The base clause establishes $0$ as the left identity; the recursive
clause formalizes addition as iterated succession. Thus, computing
$n + m$ amounts to stepping the successor function $n$ times starting
from $m$.
